correctness.rationale: The block space decomposition yields reciprocal trace contributions (x-1)/q and (y-1)/p plus (p+q)/(pq-xy), with cancellation exactly matching an empty block. At fixed x+y on balanced parts the strict dependence on xy gives both equal endpoint minima, with no interior ties. Direct rational evaluation gives the frozen witness arrays (19/12,7/4,3/2), (2/3,1,1) and (251/72,41/12,7/2), respectively. For fixed p,k the all-large-part allocation costs q/(pk) extra at leading order; all positive counts reduce to g(a)=a/p+1/a at order one. Its adjacent difference changes sign at a(a+1)=p. In the repaired theorem the adjacent tied candidates on p=r(r+1) have next coefficient difference (2k-3(r+1))/(r+1). When it is zero the following coefficient difference is (r-1)^2/4, which selects r unless r=1. Direct substitution at r=1,k=3 gives both costs (q-1)/2, and the leading-order gap excludes every other count eventually. The exact asymptotic remainder is uniform over the finite eventual candidate set.
residual_risks: Finite tests provide no general q cutoff. The result is fixed p,k before taking q large; r~sqrt(p) is not a simultaneous limit of the graph sizes.

value.rationale: Resolving the eventual optimal allocation for every fixed small-side size and budget is a structural result for a canonical two-part noisy consensus model. The limit explains the allocation scale, and the higher-order comparison decides actual optimizer classes on the locus where the leading-order problem is ambiguous. This is not a retabulation of the already known witnesses, nor just inversion of the original matrix.
residual_risks: No claim about general edge weights, noisy leaders, other objective functions, or simultaneously growing p,k,q.
